answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a stake that grows with the value it handles, like a sparrow guarding one nest. New agents start on a low trust ridge: they may only trade small amounts until they build a verifiable history of completed work. That history becomes the oasis honest agents gather around, since counterparties prefer agents with a track record, so a fresh fake identity starts with nothing. Creating thousands of identities costs real capital each, and fraud forfeits the stake, so flooding the network stops paying.
